ga.text: General and Administrative Expenses. The increase of $136.3 thousand was driven primarily by higher professional services.

nonop.text: Other Income, Net. The decrease of $0.2 million was primarily due to lower interest income resulting from lower interest rates and a lower carrying balance of short-term marketable securities.

ocf.text: Operating Activities. Net cash used in operating activities decreased $2.2 million primarily driven by a $2.7 million favorable change in working capital, partially offset by a $0.5 million increase in net loss adjusted for non-cash items. The favorable working capital change was primarily due to a smaller decrease in accrued expenses ($0.3 million in 2026 compared to $2.6 million in 2025), collections of collaboration receivables ($0.9 million inflow in 2026 compared to a $0.6 million outflow in 2025), and a decrease in tax and other receivables ($0.2 million inflow in 2026 compared to a $1.2 million outflow in 2025). These were partially offset by a $1.2 million unfavorable change in accounts payable (a $0.7 million decrease in 2026 compared to a $0.5 million increase in 2025) and the $1.25 million Senju option fee received in 2025, with no comparable receipt in 2026. Net loss increased $1.9 million, to $6.2 million from $4.3 million. Of that increase, $1.5 million was the non-cash change in fair value of contingent consideration: a $0.1 million charge in 2026 compared to a $1.3 million gain in 2025. Net cash used in operating activities for 2026 includes $835,000 received from CKD, which is the $1.0 million upfront payment net of Korean withholding tax.

wc.text: Our principal liquidity needs have historically been for acquisitions, working capital, research and development, and capital expenditures. While we anticipate having sufficient cash to fund currently planned operations into late 2027, excluding the technology transfer milestone, we will need additional financing to support our future operations as we develop and work toward the commercialization of new products. We will seek to fund our operations through a combination of public or private sales of equity, debt financings, license and development agreements, non-dilutive grants and other sources, which may include collaborations with third parties.

intro.text: We are a clinical-stage specialty pharmaceutical company developing and commercializing therapies for the treatment of retinal diseases. We are developing KIO-301, with an initial focus on patients with later stages of vision loss due to retinitis pigmentosa (collectively including any and all sub-forms, "RP"). KIO-301 is a potential vision-restoring small molecule that acts as a “photoswitch” specifically created to restore vision in patients with inherited and age-related degenerative retinal diseases, including RP. We completed a Phase 1b clinical trial in September 2023 and presented topline results in November 2023 at the American Academy of Ophthalmology Annual Meeting. The full data package triggered multiple discussions with various potential pharmaceutical partners.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
